points.t: A **raised, wandering, very itchy serpiginous line** on the foot, buttock or hand after tropical beach or soil exposure.
**Dog / cat hookworm larvae** burrow into human skin but can’t complete their life cycle, so wander in the epidermis.
Single-dose **oral ivermectin** or **albendazole 3 days** (unlicensed; specialist / ID advice) + antihistamine.
Secondary infection, and **larva currens (*Strongyloides*)**, especially before steroids or in the immunosuppressed.

points: Animal faeces → eggs on **warm, moist sand** → larvae penetrate skin when **barefoot**, sitting or lying on sand.
Larvae can’t cross the basement membrane, stay epidermal and **die in weeks–months**; the track is the reaction.
Not spread person to person; occasional UK cases in gardeners.

features.lead: A track that moves day by day.
points: Tingling at entry within hours; track **days–weeks** later.
**2–3 mm wide, raised, serpiginous**, red or skin-coloured (hypo- or hyperpigmented on darker skin).
**Intensely itchy**; moves **mm to a few cm a day**; the larva lies **1–2 cm beyond** the visible end.
Sites: **feet** (soles, toe webs, dorsum), hands, buttocks, knees, trunk.
Variants: multiple loops, **vesicles / bullae**, **hookworm folliculitis** (buttocks). Systemically well.

visuals.caption: Cutaneous larva migrans: a thin raised winding track on the sole; the larva itself sits just beyond the visible end, which is why freezing the track fails.
visuals.alt: Sole of foot with a winding red track and a magnified larva at its tip

points: Migrating itchy track + barefoot warm-climate exposure.
Fast-moving, perianal / buttock or recurrent eruption.

cards.name: Larva currens (Strongyloides)
cards.clue: Fast (**5–10 cm / hour**), urticarial band, perianal / buttocks / trunk, recurs for years; **hyperinfection with steroids**.

cards.name: Tinea
cards.clue: Annular scaly edge that doesn’t creep daily; KOH +.

cards.name: Jellyfish sting
cards.clue: Immediate painful whip marks after swimming.

cards.name: Scabies burrows
cards.clue: Short (< 1 cm) burrows in web spaces; household itch.

manage.lead: Primary care can manage most cases; resolves in 2–8 weeks untreated.

points: Non-sedating antihistamine (sedating at night per licence), emollients, short nails.
Mild–moderate topical steroid for eczematous change, **only once not larva currens**.

rx.dose: 200 micrograms/kg orally, single dose (nearest 3 mg tablet)
rx.dur: Once; repeat next day or after 1–2 weeks if it fails
rx.note: Usually unlicensed / imported; empty stomach; avoid in pregnancy / breastfeeding; < 15 kg not established.
Unlicensed for CLM; with fatty food; avoid in pregnancy; children > ~2 years.

points: 10–15% thiabendazole or albendazole ointment three times daily 1–2 weeks for single early tracks / when oral drugs unsuitable.

limits.t: Don’t: larva is ahead of the track.
Single 100 mg dose is **not** adequate for CLM.

items.t: Features of **larva currens**, especially if steroids or immunosuppression are planned.
Diagnostic doubt, widespread disease / folliculitis, treatment failure, pregnancy, child < 15 kg, wheeze or eosinophilia.

pearls.t: Larva **migrans** creeps (animal, dead end); larva **currens** runs (human *Strongyloides*, persists, **disseminates with steroids**).
Prevention: shoes on beaches where dogs roam; lie on a mat or sunbed; dry towels indoors.
Ivermectin: empty stomach with water; mild GI upset, dizziness.

quiz.q: Why does freezing the track fail?
quiz.a: The larva is 1–2 cm beyond the visible end.

quiz.q: Fast urticarial perianal track recurring for years?
quiz.a: Larva currens (Strongyloides): serology before any steroids.
